parts.text: A student investigates the extension of a spring and uses it to determine the weight of a metre rule. The spring is shown full size in Fig. 1.1 and Fig. 1.2. Fig. 1.1 shows the spring without any load. Fig. 1.2 shows the spring with a load of 1.0 N suspended from it. Fig. 1.1 Fig. 1.2

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) On Fig. 1.1, measure the length l 0 of the spring without any load. l 0 = ......................................................... cm On Fig. 1.2, measure the stretched length l S of the spring. l S = ......................................................... cm [2]

ms.label: 1(a)
ms.text:
l0 = 2(.0) (cm) and lS = 6.2 (cm)
both to 1 decimal place

ms.label: 1(b)
ms.text:
suitable method e.g.
measure distance from bench at each end and check equal

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student moves load W to distances d = 20.0 cm, d = 30.0 cm, d = 40.0 cm, d = 50.0 cm and d = 60.0 cm from the pivot. She reads the length l of the spring for each value of d . Her readings are shown in Table 1.1. Table 1.1 d / cm l / cm 20.0 6.2 30.0 7.1 40.0 7.6 50.0 8.3 60.0 9.0

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Using the values from Table 1.1, plot a graph of l / cm ( y -axis) against d / cm ( x -axis). Start the axes at the origin (0,0). 0 0 [4]

ms.label: 1(c)(i)
ms.text:
graph:
•
axes labelled with quantity and unit
•
appropriate scales (occupying at least ½ grid)
•
plots all correct to ½ small square and precise plots
•
line well-judged and thin and extended to axis

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate W R , the weight of the metre rule, using your value of L from (c)(ii) , the values of l 0 and l S from (a) and the equation W R = 2( L – l 0 ) ( l S – l 0 ) × k where k = 1.0 N. W R = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 1(c)(iii)
ms.text: WR in range 1.3 to 1.6 and with unit of N

ms.label: 1(d)(i)
ms.text:
suspend load from loop of thread /
any other suitable method to avoid standing load over marks on rule

ms.label: 1(d)(ii)
ms.text:
valid source of uncertainty e.g.
test load not exactly 1.0 N /
spring extension not linear /
metre rule not uniform
